# Disposable username and email component tests

Use only an isolated local backend on `127.0.0.1:3540/3541`, with a fresh database, no provider credentials, `--disable-beacon`, and `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` set in the backend before synchronization. Extract the catalog-selected auth archive to `authpkg` inside a disposable copy of this fixture and verify its bytes. Copy `email-fixture.ts.txt` to `authpkg/src/components/email/fixture.ts`; that seed/probe module is test-only and never enters the archive. Install dependencies in the disposable copy, then use `CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_URL` and a disposable local admin key to run `convex dev --once --typecheck disable --codegen disable`. Run `python3 test.py` and stop only the backend you started. The sender is an inert local mutation and never contacts an email provider.

The test seeds 201 attributed verified emails and challenges, races real component completion/start with email fencing and races username setting with username fencing, verifies batch bounds, replay, an unaffected user, an attributed recovery challenge, and a retained unattributed custom challenge. The synthetic seed is deliberately not a product endpoint. The test does not prove all normal auth flows, a live email delivery, other components, or complete account deletion.

The combined product runner is reserved for the assigned `127.0.0.1:3490/3491` pair; it refuses occupied ports and requires a clean committed checkout. It snapshots the exact commit, verifies installed auth against the catalog-selected archive, extracts that archive into a disposable project, uses other installed dependencies read-only, starts and stops its own backend, and uses an outbound-denying sandbox, fresh isolated environment, disabled beacon and telemetry, and blank Boat key before sync. Other provider credentials are absent from the allowlisted environment. It retains source, database and logs under `/tmp/disposabl-auth-product-*`, stops owned processes on cancellation or low disk, and uses no shared backend. Its loopback URL is not proof of ownership: invoke only through the runner after exclusive allocation; never point the test at an existing service.

```sh
CONVEX_LOCAL_BINARY="$HOME/.cache/convex/binaries/precompiled-2026-10-22-1447815/convex-local-backend" \
  python3 packages/tests/fixtures/auth-identity-erasure-convex/run-product.py
```

The runner tests the actual product operator handler with synthetic users and inert fixtures: rollback after four fences, concurrent batches, username/email/challenges, another user and re-registration denial. Unattributed challenges, provider cleanup and whole-account deletion remain unverified. Install the candidate's exact selected archive in the owned checkout first; preparation does not itself establish an upgraded-auth runtime pass. It requires at least 2.5 GiB free and retains all output.

The `email-flow` fixture mounts the real auth core, password, username and email components and the actual `setupEmailPassword` methods from the candidate. Its sender is a local internal mutation that stores synthetic messages only; the test reads the generated links from that private disposable database. In a separate disposable copy, install Convex and the catalog-selected local archive, start a fresh loopback backend, set `E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` before sync, deploy the fixture, and run `python3 test.py`. The compiled package was exercised through its normal exports; a second run mounted the extracted candidate source. The test verifies unaffected signup, email verification, login, password change and recovery, plus rejection of a pending recovery, fresh recovery, login and password change for the fenced user. A recovery challenge is intentionally created with no user attribution: denial after verified-email removal does not establish deletion of that challenge. No email is delivered and no provider is contacted.
